description: Ancestry of the cruciferous vegetables as a graph. Every node is a clade, a species, a crop lineage (a branch of cultivated forms inside a species) or a vegetable; every edge points from ancestor to descendant. Edge types: `descent` (branching between clades and species, from the Open Tree of Life), `hybrid-parent` (a species formed by two parent species combining genomes: the Triangle of U and ×Raphanobrassica), `domestication` (a cultivated branch inside a species), `selection` (a crop selected from that branch) and `cross` (a crop bred from two crops). Hybrids and crosses have two parents, so this is a network, not a single tree. Each vegetable has `lineage`: every path from the family root to it, written out. `confidence` marks how settled a step is: established, likely or debated. Genomes: A = B. rapa, B = black mustard, C = B. oleracea, R = radish.

nodes.note: Open Tree groups horseradish with Lepidium; WFO puts horseradish in tribe Cardamineae with watercress and land cress, so this grouping is uncertain.

nodes.name: Brassiceae
nodes.note: The cabbage tribe: almost all major crucifer crops.

nodes.note: Black mustard's branch, split from the rest of Brassiceae, which is why WFO now puts it in its own genus, Mutarda.

nodes.name: Brassica A + C genomes
nodes.note: B. rapa (A) and B. oleracea (C) split from a common ancestor a few million years ago; their genomes are still similar enough to combine in hybrids.
